raw_segments.text: Alexey Fyodorovich, that's true, of course, and you'll have time to quarrel and separate
a thousand times in a year and a half.
Though it's such nonsense, it's a great blow to me.
I feel like Famyusov in the last scene of Sorrow from Wit.
You are Tchatsky and she is Sofia, and only fancy I've run down to meet you on the stairs,
and in the play the fatal scene takes place on the staircase.
So this is the explanation of her dreadful night and her hysterics of late.
It means love to the daughter but death to the mother.
I might as well be in my grave at once.
And a more serious matter still, what is this letter she has written?
Show it me at once, at once.
